# Edinburgh market & audience

The scale of the Edinburgh Fringe and the audience behaviour EdFringeNow is built
for. Two decisions live here, not one: the in-the-moment "what can I make right
now" (the home site, *Fringe Discover*) and the weeks-earlier "which shows, which
dates" (the planner at `/plan`). Compiled once, refined in place.

Scope note (2026-09-01): the product's ambition is no longer Edinburgh-bound —
the owner's direction is to grow EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product.
This page stays the **Edinburgh** evidence base; the wider comedy-festival
market it would expand into is surveyed on
[festival-circuits/](../festival-circuits/README.md), and the
city-pattern question on
[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md).

## Key insights

- 2026 delivered 4,232 shows, 2.81m tickets (+8% YoY), and broke the single-day attendance record set in 2019.
- Average ticket is £13, and 1,253 shows are free or pay-what-you-want — nearly a third of the programme.
- 37% of people struggle to pick a show. Two thirds buy just one ticket.
- 78% come to see something they would not normally — they want surprise, not better filters.
- A third of the audience lives in Edinburgh. Two thirds travel in and plan months ahead.
- Beds may pick the dates, not shows — over half cannot find an affordable room nearby.
- Nobody has data on how people choose in the street. Not us, not anyone.

## Scale

### 2026 festival (7–31 August 2026, now complete)

**Final, from the Fringe Society's [closing release](https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/edinburgh-festival-fringe-2026-concludes-with-its-80th-anniversary-firmly-in-sight/)
(31 August 2026):** **4,232 shows** across **306 venues**, **61,277
performances**, artists from **77 countries** — **2,805,395 tickets issued**,
an **8% rise on 2025**. The same release records a new single-day record:
**over 164,000 tickets issued on Saturday 15 August**, 1% above the previous
peak (Saturday 17 August 2019). **1,864 accredited industry from 63
countries** and **1,091 accredited media from 30 countries** (702 of them
reviewers) attended — a finer, larger breakdown than the opening-day "over
1,600 industry and media from 53 countries" estimate below, which this
supersedes for headcount and country split.

**Opening-day release (7 August 2026)**, kept for the figures the closing
release doesn't restate:

- **4,206 shows** across **299 venues**, **over 60,000 performances**, artists
  from **74 countries**, plus 14 country showcases and four spotlight projects.
- **440 free shows** and **813 pay-what-you-want/can shows** — 1,253 together,
  close to 30% of the programme. The **average ticket price is £13**.
- Genre split at the 4 June launch: **1,401 comedy**, **1,025 theatre**, **168
  musicals and opera** (not restated in either release).

**The gap between the two releases is itself a finding.** 26 more shows, 7
more venues, 3 more countries and roughly 1,277 more performances appear
between the 7 August opening-day count and the 31 August close — so a Fringe
count is not final on opening day either; it keeps moving through the run.

**Correction — the launch snapshot undercounts, and this page had it backwards.**
Until this pass the page recorded 3,649 shows / 258 venues / 53,884 performances
/ 71 countries and concluded that 2026 was **"smaller than 2025 on both counts
(3,893 shows / 301 venues)"**. That conclusion was wrong, because it compared a
*programme-launch snapshot* with a *delivered festival*. The Society states that
**a further 553 shows registered after the printed programme launched on 4
June** — so the June number was ~15% short of the opening-day one, and 2026 in
fact finished **larger** than 2025 on both counts (4,232 vs 3,893 shows, 306
vs 301 venues, per the 31 August close). The 4 June figures are kept above
only as the launch-day genre split; they are not the festival's size. The
general lesson for anything that reads
these numbers: **a Fringe count is only final once the festival opens**, and
registration continues right up to it — and, the 2026-09-11 pass above found,
a little further still, into the festival itself.

This is still two orders of magnitude more than any one visitor can see.

### 2025 festival (still the newest site-traffic and review data)

- **3,893 shows** across **301 venues**, **53,942 performances**, artists from
  **62 countries**.
- **~2.6 million tickets** issued (2,604,404) — roughly flat on 2024, still below
  the 2019 pre-pandemic peak of about 3 million. (Superseded as the newest
  ticket count 2026-09-11: 2026's own 2,805,395, above.)
- **edfringe.com took over 3 million visits and 37 million page views**, and
  ~4,300 professional reviews were uploaded to the site to help audiences choose
  — no 2026 equivalent found yet, so these two figures are still the newest
  on the page.

This scale is the product premise: the official programme is a catalogue that
rewards planning ahead and overwhelms the person deciding in the moment.

### A Fringe-only impact study, commissioned but not yet published

Every independent audience study found so far — including the ETAG/Festivals
Edinburgh impact studies from 2011 and 2015/16 — measured **all** the Edinburgh
festivals together, never the Fringe on its own. That changes in 2026: the
University of Glasgow announced an AHRC-funded study, led by Professor Murray
Pittock, examining the Fringe's *own* economic and social impact specifically —
jobs, businesses, tourism and the longer-term value of careers that start at the
festival. Its announcement is also the first source found here to give an
attendee headcount distinct from ticket volume: **~750,000 attendees** issuing
the 2025 season's 2.6m tickets and supporting an estimated **3,000 jobs**. Both
its figures are the 2025 season's — the 2026 totals above supersede them as
ticket counts, but no 2026 attendee headcount has been published, so ~750,000
remains the only figure of its kind on this page. It is consistent with the
[two-thirds-buy-one-ticket finding](#the-overwhelm--decision-problem) below:
repeat attendance plausibly accounts for the gap between attendee and ticket
counts.

### The Fringe is not all of August

The page's scale figures — and the product built on them — cover one festival.
Seven others run concurrently: the International Festival (147 performances),
the Military Tattoo (nightly), the Deaf Festival (80+ events), the Film Festival
(38 features), the Art Festival (40+ mostly-free exhibitions), the Book Festival
(~600 events) and Fringe by the Sea. Roughly 900 further events, overlapping the
Fringe almost completely in time and largely in place.

That changes the overwhelm problem's shape rather than only its size. The Fringe
is ~80% of August's events, so any relevance- or proximity-ranked list shows a
Fringe-only city; and the non-Fringe events are the *scarcer* ones — a Fringe
show plays ~25 times, a Book Festival author appears once. The programme's scale
buries exactly what cannot be seen twice. Dates, counts, locations, the six
different shapes an "event" takes across these festivals, and whether the data is
obtainable are all worked through on
[edinburgh-festival-season/](../edinburgh-festival-season/README.md).

## The overwhelm / decision problem

Fringe Society audience data puts numbers on it:

- **37% of audiences struggled to pick a show** to go and see.
- **Two thirds of ticket buyers bought only one ticket** — for most of the
  audience the Fringe is a single decision, not a curated run of shows.
- **78% came to the Fringe to see something they wouldn't go and see otherwise** —
  the appetite is for discovery, not for a known quantity.

The standard advice around that, consistent across guides and relevant to both
surfaces:

- With more than 3,800 shows, choosing "can feel like a daunting task"; the
  advice is to lean on filters, star ratings and reviews, and to **embrace
  serendipity** — the show you'd never have booked is often the one people still
  talk about.
- **Leave travel time.** Edinburgh is compact but August streets are not; guides
  repeat that venues which look close together are not close in August — the
  reachability constraint Fringe Discover makes first-class rather than an
  afterthought.
- **Two to three shows a day** is the pace commonly advised as comfortable —
  leaving room to eat, walk, and stand still.
- **Don't fill the day.** Fringe CEO Tony Lankester's "rule of thirds" — about a
  third of the time pre-planned, the rest left open — alongside reporting that
  visitors who combined structured planning with open time were more satisfied
  than those who over-scheduled.

That last point is load-bearing here: the gaps a planner deliberately leaves are
exactly the gaps the live surface exists to fill.

## Two crowds, not one

This page previously described a single audience (the in-the-moment one) because
it was seeded from the *Fringe Discover* brief. The repo now ships two front
ends — the mobile-first home site and the desktop-first planner at `/plan` — and
they serve different people, or the same people in different states.

### A. Live, in-festival — "what can I make right now"

- **On the ground, deciding for the next hour or two.** Location, travel mode and
  the next commitment are the constraints; the catalogue is noise.
- **A third of the audience lives in Edinburgh** — locals have no trip to plan and
  no accommodation to book, and decide close to the moment by construction.
- **Same-day supply is a real channel, and an in-person one.** The Half Price Hut
  sells same-day (and next-morning) tickets from the Fringe Box Office only — not
  online, not in the app — opening 12 August in 2026, 10:00–18:00 daily.
- **Walk-up availability is not constant across the run.** Guides report walk-ups
  are easy in the opening week and that by weeks two and three popular shows —
  comedy headliners especially — sell out days in advance. The live surface's
  usefulness therefore moves with the calendar as well as the hour.
- **How the decision is actually made in the street is undocumented.** Posters,
  Royal Mile flyering, star ratings and word of mouth clearly drive a large share
  of it, but practitioners writing about Fringe marketing state plainly that
  nobody knows what works — there is no measured breakdown of in-the-moment
  discovery channels to cite.

### B. Trip planners optimising around favourite shows

- **Two thirds of the audience come from outside Edinburgh** — they choose dates,
  book beds and travel, and assemble a show list long before August.
- **Audiences now engage months ahead.** Reporting on how the Fringe audience has
  changed describes a 2026 audience that follows artists online, votes in polls
  and treats the festival as a live-entertainment marketplace well before August —
  a marked shift from the "turn up and grab a flyer" Fringe of a decade ago.
- **Accommodation binds *which dates* a trip can happen**, not as a footnote:
  coverage of the festival's accommodation crisis reports over half of people
  hoping to attend could not find an affordable place to stay within a 90-minute
  commute. Dates get chosen against beds as much as against shows — something the
  planner's "pick my best dates" currently ignores.
- **The favourites list is the planner's raw material, and it lives elsewhere.**
  Shows are favourited on edfringe.com and saved in the official app's *My
  Planner* (which syncs to a personal calendar). Getting that list *out* as a CSV
  is served by a third-party Chrome extension ("EdFringe Favourites to CSV",
  updated per festival year); no native edfringe.com CSV export is documented.
  The planner's front door depends on an export path we do not own.
- **The programme launch is the season's starting gun.** The 2026 programme went
  live on 4 June 2026, with shows revealed in batches from 11 February — so
  planning demand exists for months before any live demand can.

### The same person, at different hours

These are not necessarily two populations. The rule-of-thirds advice describes one
visitor who pre-plans part of a day and leaves the rest open; the planner serves
that first third and the live surface the other two. What differs is not identity
but **state** — horizon, device, inputs, and what "correct" even means. Those
differences are worked through on their own page:
[audience-divergence/](../audience-divergence/README.md). Nothing on this page
should be read as implying one merged requirement set.

## Audience segments (product-brief hypotheses)

From the product brief (`docs/product-spec.md`, an internal hypothesis not yet
externally validated): visitors mid-festival on foot without a fixed plan; people
with a _gap_ between commitments; locals and tourists intimidated by the
programme's size. Decisive in the moment rather than researchers, with an
emotional target of "delight + relief."

Those segments describe crowd **A** only — the brief predates `/plan`, and no
equivalent written segmentation exists for the trip-planning crowd. The partial
external evidence for crowd B is the block above (two thirds non-resident,
months-ahead engagement, accommodation-first date choice); a validated
segmentation for either crowd remains an open question.

## Sources

- [#MixItUp at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe and discover your new favourite show (edfringe.com, 7 August 2026)](https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/mixitup-at-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe-and-discover-your-new-favourite-show/) — the opening-day release: 4,206 shows, 299 venues, 74 countries, 60,000+ performances, 440 free and 813 pay-what-you-want shows, £13 average ticket, 1,600+ accredited industry/media from 53 countries, and 553 shows registered since the 4 June programme launch.
- [Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2026 concludes with its 80th anniversary firmly in sight (edfringe.com, 31 August 2026)](https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/edinburgh-festival-fringe-2026-concludes-with-its-80th-anniversary-firmly-in-sight/) — the closing release: 4,232 shows, 306 venues, 77 countries, 61,277 performances, 2,805,395 tickets issued (+8% on 2025), a new single-day record (164,000+ tickets, Sat 15 Aug), 1,864 accredited industry (63 countries) and 1,091 accredited media (30 countries, 702 reviewers).
- [The 2026 Edinburgh Festival Fringe programme is now live (edfringe.com)](https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/mixitup-with-the-2026-edinburgh-festival-fringe-programme/)

- [Key dates for your diary in the lead-up to Fringe 2026 (edfringe.com)](https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/key-dates-for-your-diary-in-the-lead-up-to-fringe-2026/)
- [Edinburgh Festival Fringe issues over 2.6 million tickets across 3,893 shows (BroadwayWorld)](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Edinburgh-Festival-Fringe-Issues-Over-26-Million-Tickets-Across-3893-Shows-20250826)
- [Fringe Society releases 2025 ticket and audience data (WhatsOnStage)](https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/edinburgh-festival-fringe-society-releases-ticket-and-audience-data-as-2025-event-concludes_1692055/)

- [How to use your audience data with a purpose: the Edinburgh Festival Fringe (Thrive)](https://wewillthrive.co.uk/resources/case-studies/how-to-use-your-audience-data-with-a-purpose-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe/)

- [How to choose which shows to see at the Fringe (edfringe.com)](https://www.edfringe.com/about-us/news-and-blog/how-to-choose-which-shows-to-see-at-the-edinburgh-festival-fringe/)
- [Study to examine economic and social impact of Edinburgh Festival Fringe (University of Glasgow)](https://www.gla.ac.uk/news/headline_1266521_en.html) — Prof Murray Pittock's AHRC-funded study; ~750,000 attendees, 2.6m tickets in 2025, ~3,000 jobs supported; the first Fringe-only (not whole-cluster) impact study found.
- [Study to examine economic and social impact of Edinburgh Festival Fringe (The Scotsman)](https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/study-to-examine-economic-and-social-impact-of-edinburgh-festival-fringe-8555482) — independent corroboration of the announcement.
- [Edinburgh Festivals Impact Study Technical Report, May 2011 (ETAG)](https://www.etag.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2013/11/110520-edinburgh-festivalstechnical-report-bop_final.pdf) — read second-hand via search-engine indexing only (the domain is blocked by this environment's network egress, like every non-edfringe.com site probed on this page's sibling pages); reportedly finds substantial cross-festival attendance (figures around 50–70% depending on festival, by search-engine summary), but unverified against the primary document and now 15 years old. Cited here as a lead, not a fact — see the open question below.
- [Edinburgh Festivals 2015 Impact Study — announcement (ETAG)](https://www.etag.org.uk/2016/08/edinburgh-festivals-2015-impact-study/) — a newer (2016) whole-cluster study, 29,273 surveyed, £280m Edinburgh / £313m Scotland economic impact, 4.5m+ combined audiences; same egress-block caveat, and the search-indexed summary found no Fringe-specific crossover breakdown in it.

## Open questions

- **Sizing the two crowds.** "A third of the audience lives in Edinburgh" is the
  only hard split found; there is still no cited figure for spontaneous /
  gap-filling versus pre-planned attendance, nor for how many of the two thirds
  from outside Edinburgh are day-trippers (no accommodation decision) versus
  multi-night stays (the planner's real crowd).
- **How the in-the-moment decision is really made.** Still no measured breakdown
  of in-street discovery channels — the honest current answer is that nobody has
  the data. A small first-party observation (even n=20 on the Royal Mile) would
  beat the citation vacuum.
- **When planning happens.** No cited series for advance-versus-same-day
  purchasing, or for how sales pace across the run. This decides whether the
  planner is a June–July product or an all-August one.
- **Does the favourites list have a native export?** The third-party CSV
  extension exists; whether edfringe.com itself offers an export — and how many
  people ever produce one — is unconfirmed, and the planner's intake depends on
  it. (Sharpened 2026-08-09: a rival planner, edfringeplanner.co.uk, advertises
  that it "takes your favourites from edfringe.com", so *some* route out exists —
  whether it is a native export, the same extension, or a login-scrape is
  unknown. See [competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).)
- **Do the price figures survive contact with the data?** New this pass: a £13
  average ticket and 1,253 free / pay-what-you-want shows are the first cited
  price numbers this wiki has. The product brief still says we hold no price
  beyond a free/paid flag, and the scraped GraphQL only carries `priceType` —
  so this is a published aggregate we cannot currently reproduce or attribute
  per show. Whether the official Listings API's `price` field would close that
  is on [edinburgh-festival-season/](../edinburgh-festival-season/README.md).
- **How much does the programme still move during the run?** Answered in part
  2026-09-11: it does — 26 more shows, 7 more venues and 3 more countries
  appear between the 7 August opening-day count and the 31 August close. What
  remains open is the *shape* of that movement — net registrations, or a mix
  of additions and cancellations/pulls — which decides how often the catalogue
  must be refreshed to stay honest through the run, not just before it.
- **Accommodation as a planning input.** No authoritative price/availability
  series found (guide-site figures only). If beds constrain dates more than shows
  do, "pick my best dates" optimises the wrong variable — worth evidence before
  acting on it.
- **Do Fringe-goers attend a second festival?** Narrowed 2026-08-16, not
  answered: no *Fringe-specific* crossover figure was found with byte-verified
  sourcing (this environment's network egress blocks every source domain that
  might carry one). The closest lead is second-hand and imperfect: ETAG's
  2011 and 2015/16 Edinburgh Festivals Impact Studies both measured audience
  behaviour across **all** the Edinburgh festivals together, never the Fringe
  specifically, and only the older one's search-indexed summary mentions a
  cross-festival attendance figure at all (~50-70% depending on festival) —
  unverifiable and now 15 years stale. The 2026 Pittock study (see Scale,
  above) is the one to watch: if it surveys audiences rather than only
  desk-modelling economic flows, it may be the first source able to answer
  this with current, Fringe-specific data. Still matters for the same reason:
  the case for widening the product past the Fringe rests on an unmeasured
  assumption that the eight August audiences would go to each other's
  festivals if they knew.
- **When will the Pittock study publish, and what will it measure?**
  Announced 2026 (University of Glasgow, AHRC-funded); no publication date or
  methodology detail found. Worth a follow-up pass once it lands.
- **Does the record single-day attendance (164,000+ tickets, Sat 15 Aug 2026)
  track a single cause** — a headline show, a weekend/weekday pattern, weather —
  or is it simply proportional to the festival's own 8% YoY growth? New this
  pass; unexamined.

## Growth log

- **2026-07-22** — initial seed: 2025 scale figures (shows / venues / tickets),
  the overwhelm-and-serendipity decision context, and the travel-time constraint;
  audience segments flagged as unvalidated product-brief hypotheses. Sources
  cited.
- **2026-07-28** — took the `/plan` surface into account and split the page from
  one audience into two crowds (live in-festival; trip planners optimising around
  favourites). Added 2026 scale figures (3,649 shows / 258 venues / 53,884
  performances / 71 countries, 7–31 Aug) alongside the retained 2025 ticket data;
  added cited decision-difficulty data (37% struggled to pick, two thirds bought
  a single ticket, 78% came for something they wouldn't otherwise see), the "rule
  of thirds" / don't-over-schedule finding, the same-day and walk-up supply
  picture, the non-resident share, the accommodation constraint on date choice,
  and the third-party favourites-CSV dependency. Recorded that the product
  brief's segments cover crowd A only. Open questions rewritten in both
  directions. Requirements implication (two requirement tracks, not one) left for
  human review — see the audience-divergence page.
- **2026-07-29** — added the page's `## Key insights` header: seven terse lines
  distilled from what the page already says (scale, the decision-difficulty
  figures, the two crowds, the accommodation constraint, the evidence gaps).
  Header only: no claim, citation or open question changed.
- **2026-07-31** — recorded that the market is eight overlapping August
  festivals, not one: added "The Fringe is not all of August" under Scale (~900
  further events, the Fringe at ~80% of volume, and the inversion that the
  scarcer events are the ones volume ranking buries), pointing at the new
  edinburgh-festival-season page for dates, counts, locations and data availability. Key
  insight 1 rewritten from the year-on-year shrink to the cluster; the shrink
  claim stays in the body. Added the cross-festival attendance open question.
  Requirements implication left for human review.
- **2026-08-09** — spot-checked the 2026 scale figures two days into the festival
  and found them stale *and* wrong in direction. Replaced the 4 June
  programme-launch snapshot (3,649 shows / 258 venues / 53,884 performances / 71
  countries) with the Fringe Society's opening-day release (4,206 shows / 299
  venues / 60,000+ performances / 74 countries), and corrected — with the reason
  kept in the body rather than deleted — the page's "smaller than 2025 on both
  counts" conclusion, which had compared a launch snapshot against a delivered
  festival; 553 shows registered after the programme launched, so 2026 finished
  larger than 2025 on shows. Added the first cited price data in this wiki (£13
  average ticket; 440 free plus 813 pay-what-you-want shows, ~30% of the
  programme) and the 1,600+ accredited industry/media figure. Key insights 1 and
  2 rewritten; the "don't fill the day" bullet dropped from the header to stay
  inside the seven-bullet cap — it is unchanged in the body, and the sharper
  version of it already leads
  [audience-divergence/](../audience-divergence/README.md). Three open questions
  added (price reproducibility, in-run programme churn, a sharpened
  favourites-export question); no requirement touched. The superseded figures
  also propagate to edinburgh-festival-season and festmaxxing-environments, both
  corrected in the same pass.
- **2026-08-16** — worked the "do Fringe-goers attend a second festival?" open
  question and found a genuinely new lead rather than an answer: a University
  of Glasgow study (Prof Murray Pittock, AHRC-funded) announced in 2026 is the
  first impact study found that examines the Fringe on its own, rather than
  bundled with the other Edinburgh festivals as ETAG's 2011 and 2015/16 studies
  did — added under Scale, with the first attendee-headcount figure (~750,000,
  distinct from the 2.6m ticket count) found in this research, plus ~3,000 jobs
  supported. The cross-festival open question is narrowed, not closed: the only
  cross-festival attendance figure found is second-hand (via search-engine
  indexing, this environment's egress proxy blocking the source domain) and 15
  years stale, so it is recorded as an unverified lead rather than a fact. New
  open question added for when the Pittock study publishes. Spot-checked
  competitor-landscape and festival-cities-beyond-edinburgh (the pages last
  touched, 2026-08-11; the latter is now
  [festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md)) for claims this pass's research might supersede — found
  nothing to correct; their unreached competitor-site open questions remain
  blocked by the same egress proxy as before, not new. No requirement touched.
- **2026-09-01** — added the scope note under the title: the owner's direction
  is now a festival-planning product rather than an Edinburgh-only one, with
  the wider comedy-festival market owned by the new
  [festival-circuits/](../festival-circuits/README.md) page. This
  page's own claims, figures and open questions are untouched — it remains the
  Edinburgh evidence base.
- **2026-09-01** — renamed from `market-and-audience/` to
  `edinburgh-market-and-audience/` on the owner's direction: the page's own
  scope note pins it as the Edinburgh evidence base, and the name now says
  so. Content unchanged; all inbound links updated in the same change.
- **2026-09-11** — refreshed the 2026 scale section with the Fringe Society's
  closing release (31 August, the festival having ended): 4,232 shows / 306
  venues / 77 countries / 61,277 performances / 2,805,395 tickets (+8% on
  2025), plus a new single-day attendance record (164,000+ tickets, Sat 15
  Aug, edging out 2019's prior peak) and a finer industry/media breakdown
  (1,864 industry from 63 countries; 1,091 media from 30 countries, 702
  reviewers) that supersedes the opening-day "1,600+ from 53 countries"
  estimate. New finding: the count moved again between the 7 August
  opening-day figures and the close (+26 shows, +7 venues, +3 countries) —

  ticket data now supersedes it — 2025's site-traffic and review figures stay

1	# The festival circuits
2	
3	The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
4	and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
5	This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
6	EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
7	the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
8	genre. Compiled once, refined in place.
9	
10	Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
11	[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md)
12	owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
13	pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
14	the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
15	reachability — plus a deliberately light survey of the **film** festivals that
16	share the planner-complex shape (its own section below). Planner-type
17	competitors found along the way live on
18	[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).
19	
20	## Key insights
21	
22	- Only ~8 of 85 census festivals are fringe-shaped. Most of the circuit is one-night showcases with nothing to schedule.
23	- MICF is the southern Edinburgh — 803 shows, 9,164 performances, open registration — with unauthenticated JSON APIs.
24	- Leicester's operator went bust in Aug 2026 owing performers ticket money. Feb 2027 is two rival reboots.
25	- Nearly everything is annual in the same city, but brands churn: JFL survived receivership, Netflix Is A Joke is biennial.
26	- Recurrence decides planning — in film too: Fringe shows play ~14 times, Berlinale screens films up to 5×, US one-offs are terminal.
27	- Leicester and Brighton share one platform (Eventotron) and identical open APIs — one adapter reads both.
28	- No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists. The best tracker is one journalist's hand-kept page.
29	
30	## The census: a year of comedy festivals

125	
126	Not in the table: three undated entries — the **San Francisco Comedy
127	Competition** ("across the Bay Area") and **Seattle International Comedy
128	Competition** ("all month across Western Washington", November), both
129	month-long *touring competitions* rather than city takeovers, and **Just For
130	Laughs Singapore** (tbd) — plus the first 2027 confirmations (JFL Bermuda,
131	17–20 Feb 2027; SXSW, 17–20 Mar 2027). The tracker's own dates are treated
132	here as launch-time claims, not delivered totals — and the dossiers below
133	correct five of its entries against primary sources: Roundhouse actually ran
134	1–18 Aug, Greenwich has rebranded to "Comedy Garden", the "Dublin Comedy
135	Festival" is a suburban pub circuit, JFL Paris appears dead, and
136	Machynlleth (the UK's best small-town takeover) is missing entirely.
137	
138	What the census says before any per-festival research:
139	
140	- **The circuit is mostly weekend showcases.** 45 of 85 dated festivals run ≤4
141	  days, and 56 of 85 are in the US — overwhelmingly club-scale, curated or
142	  submission-based weekends where a visitor picks a headliner, not a schedule.
143	- **The fringe-length tier is small and un-American.** Only 13 festivals run
144	  ≥14 days, and the US contributes just two (SF Sketchfest and the new Fallout
145	  Fringe in Las Vegas); the other eleven are UK, Irish, Australian and NZ
146	  events — Edinburgh, Adelaide, Brighton, Melbourne, Sydney Comedy Festival,
147	  JFL Sydney, NZICF, Leicester, Aberdeen, the London Clown Festival, and the
148	  Dublin entry examined below.
149	- **Run length is a strong first classifier.** A festival long enough to need
150	  repeat performances of the same show is where a scheduling product has work
151	  to do; a weekend of one-night showcases is not. The dossiers below test that
152	  presumption festival by festival.
153	
154	## The two shapes, and what decides planner-worthiness
155	
156	The owner's framing question — which festivals behave like the Fringe and
157	which like music festivals — turns out to rest on two measurable axes, and
158	the dossiers below supply the numbers:
159	
160	1. **Parallel volume**: how many shows run at once. Edinburgh peaks in the
161	   thousands per day; MICF at ~350; Leicester's own API shows 242 on its
162	   peak Saturday; Netflix Is A Joke ~100; Sydney ~29; most of the census
163	   runs single digits. Below a few dozen parallel shows, "which can I make"
164	   stops being a problem a product needs to solve.
165	2. **Recurrence**: how many times one show plays. Edinburgh averages ~14
166	   performances per show and MICF ~11 — miss tonight, catch tomorrow, so
167	   planning is *packing*. Sydney averages 2.4 and Leicester 2.28; the US
168	   majors run one-night events almost exclusively — every clash is
169	   terminal, so planning is *triage*, and with few parallel shows it
170	   reduces to picking headliners.
171	
172	Two more axes modulate the answer: **venue geography** (a walkable core —
173	Edinburgh, MICF's CBD, Machynlleth — makes multi-show days physically
174	possible; a car city like LA or Dubai caps a day at one neighbourhood;
175	a single site has nothing to route) and **access model** (open access —
176	anyone who pays registers — is what produces uncapped supply; curation caps
177	it by construction).
178	
179	The resulting map of the census:
180	
181	- **Fringe-shaped** (open access, repeated runs, many venues, real clash
182	  grid): Edinburgh, Adelaide, **MICF**, **Brighton** (46% comedy), and
183	  **Leicester** in its short-visit variant — plus **NZICF** small and
184	  **Machynlleth** miniature. This is the entire planner-market tier, and
185	  outside Edinburgh none of it has a third-party planner
186	  ([competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md)).
187	- **Showcase-shaped** (curated one-nighters, pick-your-headliner): the JFL
188	  empire, NYCF, Sydney, Perth, Galway, Dubai, Aberdeen, Winnipeg, Halifax,
189	  Nashville, 312, and — at fringe *breadth* but one-off depth — SF
190	  Sketchfest and Netflix Is A Joke, where the planning problem is real but
191	  is scarcity-triage (nothing repeats) rather than schedule-packing.
192	- **Distinct sub-shapes the two poles don't cover**: the **badge-graze**
193	  festivals (Moontower's club binge, Del Close Marathon, SXSW) where entry
194	  is walk-in and the constraint is room capacity, not tickets; the
195	  **roving franchise** (Great Outdoors; 57 Festivals' Comedy Gardens) — one
196	  stage, touring cities; the **anti-planner compound** (Skankfest, schedule
197	  released day-of); the **touring competitions** (Boston's bracket, SF and
198	  Seattle's month-long circuits); the **TV-taping festivals** (Winnipeg,
199	  Halifax — the broadcast is the product); the **venue season** (Aberdeen,
200	  Roundhouse); the **club hub** (Tokyo, Grindstone); and the **pub circuit**
201	  wearing a festival name (the "Dublin Comedy Festival").
202	
203	The product read: **run length in the census predicts the shape but does
204	not decide it** — Sydney (35 days) and Aberdeen (16) are showcases, while
205	Machynlleth (3 days) has a denser grid than either. The deciding pair is
206	parallel volume × recurrence, and only the fringe-shaped tier scores high
207	on both.
208	
209	## The fringe-shaped tier: dossiers
210	
211	The festivals where "which of tonight's shows can I make" is a real problem —
212	long runs, repeated performances, many parallel rooms. This is the tier a
213	planning product can serve.
214	
215	### Melbourne International Comedy Festival — the southern Edinburgh
216	
217	The standout of the whole census, and the closest thing to a second Edinburgh
218	Fringe anywhere in comedy.
219	
220	- **Scale, delivered 2026** (the festival's own
221	  [40th-year wrap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/celebrating-a-record-40th-year/)):
222	  **803 shows and events, 9,164 performances, 26 days** (25 Mar–19 Apr),
223	  796,975 attendees (+13% YoY), A$26.6m box office, average paid ticket
224	  A$38.20. That is ~350 performances a day — genuinely fringe-like clash
225	  density. Launch press said "over 750 shows", so ~50 more landed after
226	  launch: the launch-undercount trap
227	  [edinburgh-market-and-audience/](../edinburgh-market-and-audience/README.md) documents holds
228	  here too.
229	- **Show model**: Edinburgh-style seasons — one show is the same hour repeated
230	  across the run (sampled runs of 7–24 performances; cheaper previews,
231	  cheap-Tuesday flags). Participation is **open registration**
232	  ([registrations open each October](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/participate/),
233	  with independent venues found via a venue finder) — the Fringe's
234	  open-access mechanism, at ~one-fifth Edinburgh's scale.
235	- **Organizer & recurrence**: its own festival organization, annual every
236	  autumn since 1987, always Melbourne, centred on Melbourne Town Hall;
237	  [self-described](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/about-us/) as "one of
238	  the three largest comedy festivals in the world, alongside Edinburgh
239	  Festival Fringe and Montreal's Just for Laughs" and "Australia's largest
240	  ticketed cultural event". Stable through a 2026 leadership handover
241	  (Susan Provan retired after 32 years;
242	  [Dylan Cole appointed CEO/Festival Director](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/news/melbourne-international-comedy-festival-appoints-dylan-cole-as-new-ceofestival-director/)).
243	  2027 dates already announced (24 Mar–18 Apr).
244	- **Venues**: 143 venue buildings in its own venues data — 66 in the CBD, the
245	  rest a suburban tail (Northcote, Box Hill…) — a walkable core plus
246	  outliers, the Edinburgh pattern loosened one notch.
247	- **Ticketing**: comedyfestival.com.au is **its own central box office** with
248	  one basket across shows (a cart API, accounts, native favourites with
249	  share-a-favourites-list); a minority of external-venue shows link out to
250	  Ticketmaster/Ticketek/Arts Centre Melbourne.
251	- **Data reachability — best in the census**: unauthenticated JSON endpoints,
252	  verified by fetch:
253	  `POST /umbraco/api/searchapi/searchShows` (826 show records for 2026, paged,
254	  with runs, performance counts, venue rooms),
255	  `GET /umbraco/api/venuesapi/getvenues` (all 143 venues with address,
256	  capacity, accessibility flags), and each show page embeds a `sessionData`
257	  JSON array with per-performance date, time, **on-sale status and
258	  sold-out/preview/cheap-night flags** — near enough 1:1 onto the fields the
259	  Edinburgh scraper already produces. A
260	  [sitemap](https://www.comedyfestival.com.au/sitemap.xml) lists every show
261	  URL.
262	- **Concurrent**: Melbourne Food & Wine Festival and the Flower & Garden Show
263	  overlap the window, with the AFL season running throughout (per
264	  [melbournetourism.org](https://www.melbournetourism.org/melbourne-events-and-festivals-calendar/))
265	  — city-draw amplifiers, though nothing on the scale of Edinburgh's August
266	  cluster.
267	- **Planner field**: the site's account favourites are the only planning tool;
268	  no current official app found (a
269	  [2010-era iPhone app](https://itwire.com/software/laugh-it-up-on-the-iphone-melbourne-international-comedy-festival-app.html)
270	  is the last trace), and no third-party planner exists — see
271	  [competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).
272	
273	### Adelaide Fringe — covered elsewhere, plus the ticketing angle
274	
275	Scale, open access and the "Mad March" cluster are on
276	[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md);
277	what this pass adds is ticketing and data. Adelaide Fringe Inc. (a
278	not-for-profit, incorporated 1975) runs **its own ticketing platform,
279	FringeTIX** — [first used in 1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_Fringe),
280	today a Rails app inside adelaidefringe.com.au with a central cart across all
281	shows and venues — and [markets that platform (AVR) to other open-access
282	festivals](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/about-us) as "the best solution for
283	collating and managing open access festivals". No public API was found
284	(probes 404/500 off-season); a scrape would target the server-rendered
285	FringeTIX listing in season. Comedy's share of the ~1,500-show programme is
286	not published —
287	[the 2026 launch](https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringefeed/news/2026-program-unveiled-with-more-than-1500-shows)
288	lists comedy first among genres with no counts.
289	
290	### NZ International Comedy Festival — one festival, two cities at once
291	
292	- **Organizer**: the [New Zealand Comedy Trust](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/the-new-zealand-comedy-trust/),
293	  a charitable not-for-profit; festival annual each May since 1995 (roots
294	  1993), 2026 = the 33rd Auckland edition and the Wellington leg's 30th.
295	- **The two-city model**: one programme, one window (1–24 May 2026), running
296	  **simultaneously** in Auckland and Wellington with region-filtered listings
297	  (plus a "Gala toe-dip" in Christchurch in 2026); some acts play a season in
298	  each city inside the window. Each city is a compact centre cluster
299	  (Auckland: Q Theatre, Basement, The Classic + big halls for headliners;
300	  Wellington: BATS' three rooms, Te Auaha, Hannah Playhouse).
301	- **Scale & model**: the Trust's steady-state description is
302	  ["over 120 show seasons, over 600 performances, around 200 comedians"](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/about-us/new-zealand-international-comedy-festival/),
303	  75,000+ attendance in 2025 — Edinburgh-style short seasons (~5 performances
304	  each), a real but small evening-choice problem (~a dozen parallel shows per
305	  city on peak nights).
306	- **Ticketing**: **no central basket** — the festival site is a catalogue that
307	  [hands buyers to the right agent per show](https://comedyfestival.co.nz/how-to-buy-tickets):
308	  Ticketmaster, Q Theatre's box office, Eventfinda or iTicket, each with its
309	  own fees. A cross-show plan means juggling up to four seller accounts.
310	- **Data**: server-rendered SilverStripe site, no JSON API found; a scrape
311	  targets the find-a-show HTML per region.
312	- **Concurrent**: May in Auckland is genuinely congested — NZ Music Month plus
313	  the Auckland Writers Festival inside the window;
314	  [The Spinoff](https://thespinoff.co.nz/pop-culture/06-05-2026/auckland-has-a-problem-everything-awesome-is-happening-in-may-all-at-once):
315	  "Auckland has a problem. Everything awesome is happening in May, all at
316	  once."
317	- **Planner field**: the official planning tool is a downloadable timetable
318	  PDF. Nothing else exists.
319	
320	### Sydney Comedy Festival — the boundary case
321	
322	Fringe-scale show count, showcase-shaped mechanics — the census's clearest
323	demonstration that show count alone doesn't decide the shape:
324	
325	- **Delivered 2026** (per the festival's wrap, carried by
326	  [The Movie Boards](https://www.themovieboards.net/2026/05/18/record-growth-and-huge-crowds-for-sydney-comedy-festival/)):
327	  **411 shows, close to 1,000 performances, 57 venues, 175,000+ attendees**
328	  over 35 days (13 Apr–17 May) — but that is **~2.4 performances per show**
329	  against MICF's ~11.4: mostly weekend-length visits, galas and showcases,
330	  not month-long seasons.
331	- **Structure**: run by [Century Entertainment](https://www.century.com.au/about/),
332	  a commercial venue group (Enmore Theatre, Comedy Store…), **curated by
333	  application**, venues scattered "from Bondi to Penrith" (a metro
334	  constellation, not a walkable core), **per-venue ticketing** with no
335	  central basket (Century venues on TicketSearch, tour venues on their own
336	  sellers), followed by a national showcase tour May–December. Concurrent:
337	  Sydney Royal Easter Show and Writers' Festival brush the window, Vivid
338	  starts just after.
339	- Century also produces the **[Perth Comedy Festival](https://www.perthcomedyfestival.com/about/)**
340	  (20 Apr–17 May 2026, ~70 gigs across 5 venues — fully showcase-shaped) on
341	  the same WordPress codebase — one scrape adapter would cover both.
342	
343	### Leicester Comedy Festival — the UK's second clash problem, operator now dead
344	
345	The February anchor of UK comedy, and this pass's most dramatic finding:
346	**the organising charity collapsed in August 2026**, weeks before this page
347	was written.
348	
349	- **Shape**: open access — "anyone can pay a fee to put on an event",
350	  registered through Eventotron
351	  ([registration page](https://comedy-festival-takepart.co.uk/how-to-register-your-show))
352	  — annual each February since 1994, same city. 2026:
353	  [700+ shows across 81 venues](https://leicestertimes.com/leicester-news/leicester-comedy-festival-launches-with-over-700-shows-celebrating-the-art-of-comedy/52061/)
354	  over 19 days, plus a kids' comedy festival. Its own events API (fetched)
355	  counts 753 shows whose bookings average **2.28 days per show** — so the
356	  clash problem is fringe-scale (**242 shows on the peak Saturday**, per the
357	  API's date taxonomy) while the *runs* are short visits, not
358	  Edinburgh-length seasons. Venues run from a city-centre core out to county
359	  village halls.
360	- **Ticketing & data**: central box office on the festival's own site — the
361	  **Eventotron** WordPress plugin plus Stripe, leaving a fully open REST API
362	  (`events.comedy-festival.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2/events`, 753 events with
363	  dates/genres/venues taxonomies, verified by fetch) — the same substrate
364	  and API shape as Brighton Fringe below: **one adapter would read both**.
365	- **The collapse**: operator Big Difference Company (charity 1135167) became
366	  insolvent and ceased trading —
367	  [its own 26 Aug 2026 statement](https://irp.cdn-website.com/b436dc39/files/uploaded/Statement+BDC+26_08_2026.docx)
368	  — with [debts over £215,000](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/22/61391/leicester_comedy_festival_charitys_debts_exceed_%c2%a3215,000)
369	  and performers owed their ticket money (the Feb 2026 festival *happened*;
370	  Wikipedia's "cancelled" lede is wrong). February 2027 is now contested by
371	  **two** efforts, sharpened this pass (2026-09-13, search-attributed — see
372	  the open question below): the **city council's own interim programme**,
373	  which its own news site describes as run with local promoters, venues and
374	  "the expertise of its own festivals and De Montfort Hall teams" while it
375	  works toward "a sustainable operation for the long-term" — not itself the
376	  festival named below — and comedians **Colin Bowles and Alex Hylton's**
377	  [**Independent Comedy Festival**](https://www.chortle.co.uk/news/2026/08/11/61247/leicester_gets_a_new_comedy_festival)
378	  (3–21 Feb 2027; named venues include The Y Theatre, Firebug, Real Ale
379	  Classroom and Oadby Royal British Legion), formed by promoters and acts
380	  the collapse left unpaid. Both use different mechanics: the council effort
381	  is a venue/promoter partnership, while the Independent Comedy Festival
382	  runs on **TixEvery**, which pays comedians directly and routes ticket
383	  revenue around any central organiser entirely — a ticketing model born
384	  directly of the collapse. For the product: the incumbent data source works
385	  today and its owner is in liquidation, and there is no single "successor"
386	  — which of two parallel efforts (or both) constitutes "Leicester" next
387	  year, and whether either exposes anything like the old Eventotron API, is
388	  still genuinely open.
389	
390	### Brighton Fringe — half of it is a comedy festival
391	
392	Already profiled as a city on
393	[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md);
394	what this pass adds is measured comedy share, mechanics and the cluster.
395	**Comedy is 46% of the live programme** — 394 of 864 events in its own
396	events API carry the Comedy genre (fetched; cross-edition genre totals give
397	42%) — making open-access, month-long Brighton effectively half a comedy
398	festival, the largest comedy event in the UK after Edinburgh with Leicester
399	gone. Central box office on brightonfringe.org itself, on the **same
400	Eventotron + Stripe substrate as Leicester** with the same open REST API
401	(the what's-on grid is client-rendered, but the API is not). Its May window
402	contains a real cluster:
403	[Brighton Festival (curated, 105 events, 1–25 May)](https://brightonfestival.org/press-office/press-release-brighton-festival-2026-launch/)
404	and [The Great Escape new-music showcase (13–16 May, 30+ venues)](https://www.livenation.co.uk/event/the-great-escape-2026-brighton-tickets-edp1637482)
405	sit wholly inside Brighton Fringe's 1–31 May.
406	
407	### Machynlleth — the small-town takeover (missing from the tracker)
408	
409	[Machynlleth Comedy Festival](https://machcomedyfest.co.uk/) is not on the
410	seed tracker at all and belongs in the census: run by producer Little
411	Wander, 15th year in 2026, **200+ shows in three days (1–3 May) in a Welsh
412	town of ~2,000 people** — ~65+ parallel-ish shows a day, a genuine clash
413	problem at miniature scale, with an official festival app. Single-curator
414	in structure, fringe-dense in feel: the reference point for the
415	"small-town takeover" model (Wells is its curated-weekend little sibling).
416	
417	## The showcase majors: dossiers
418	
419	Big festivals where the visitor picks headliners rather than solves a
420	schedule — one-night curated events, few or no repeats, tickets scattered
421	across vendors. The blunt cross-cutting finding from the US research: **no US
422	major is fringe-shaped.**
423	
424	### The Just For Laughs empire — survived receivership, showcase to the bone
425	
426	The census's nine JFL entries are one company plus its licensees, and its
427	recent history is the sharpest annual-vs-durable case in the circuit:
428	
429	- **The ownership arc**: founded 1983 (Gilbert Rozon); sold 2018 to the Howie
430	  Mandel / ICM / Bell Media / Groupe CH group after Rozon's resignation;
431	  **filed for creditor protection in March 2024** — the 2024 Montreal and
432	  Toronto festivals were cancelled outright, with
433	  [$22.5m of debt and an $800k loss to email phishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_for_Laughs)
434	  later revealed; assets acquired mid-2024 by **ComediHa!** (Sylvain
435	  Parent-Bédard's Quebec City group, per
436	  [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/quebec-entertainment-group-comediha-confirms-acquisition-of-just-for-laughs-assets/)),
437	  parent since renamed Groupe Juste pour divertir. A reduced 2025 comeback,
438	  then a full-volume 2026: the
439	  [44th Montreal edition, 15–26 July — ~250 shows, ~25 venues, 800+ artists](https://www.themain.com/articles/just-for-laughs-montreal-2026-guide),
440	  with [2027 satellite dates already published](https://comedyevent.bm/).
441	  Read: a durable annual anchor again — two years into a turnaround, its
442	  scale figures its own marketing.
443	- **The Montreal model** is three tiers, none of them fringe runs: TV-taping
444	  **galas** at Place des Arts; **curated showcase runs of 1–5 nights** (The
445	  Nasty Show, Midnight Surprise) plus premium one-offs (Letterman at up to
446	  $550, per [Cult MTL](https://cultmtl.com/2026/07/just-for-laughs-and-off-jfl-are-showcasing-hundreds-of-great-comedians-in-montreal-from-july-15-to-26/));
447	  and a huge **free outdoor** programme at Place des Festivals.
448	  [Place des Arts' "nearly two million visitors"](https://www.placedesarts.com/en/festival/just-for-laughs-festival)
449	  counts those free crowds — which is how "world's largest comedy festival"
450	  survives as a label while MICF trebles its ticketed show count. The
451	  fringe-ish annex is **OFF-JPR** (the relaunched
452	  [Zoofest](https://www.offjpr.com/), ~one-night $24–32 club sets), and the
453	  industry layer is ComedyPRO with the New Faces showcases. Everything sits
454	  in the Quartier des Spectacles — concentrated, walkable, evening slots at
455	  7:00/9:30/midnight; a missed showcase usually repeats tomorrow, so clash
456	  pain is modest.
457	- **Franchise map**: Montreal, Quebec City (the rebranded 25-year-old
458	  ComediHa! Fest, now deliberately overlapping Montreal's dates), Toronto
459	  (ex-JFL42, relaunched 2025, [24 Sep–3 Oct 2026](https://toronto.hahaha.com/))
460	  and Vancouver ([12–22 Feb, 100+ shows](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/just-for-laughs-vancouver-2026))
461	  are owned-and-operated; Sydney and Singapore run with promoter Bohm
462	  Presents ([justforlaughs.sydney](https://www.justforlaughs.sydney/) is a
463	  tour-stop model on Opera House + external venue ticketing); Bermuda,
464	  Belgium (Namur) and Switzerland are local promoters carrying the brand.
465	  **The tracker's "JFL Paris" entry appears dead** — the hahaha.com festival
466	  URL 404s and no 2026 edition was found.
467	- **Ticketing & data**: the hahaha.com family sells on its **own platform**
468	  (a proprietary "Nova" CMS with Stripe, per-city baskets and a wishlist);
469	  Sydney explicitly fans out to six external sellers. No structured API; the
470	  programme loads as client-side HTML fragments — and **listings are
471	  ephemeral: city sites were emptied within weeks of the festival ending**,
472	  so any programme capture has to happen during the on-sale window.
473	- **Concurrents**: Montreal's window near-totally overlaps the
474	  [Fantasia film festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasia_International_Film_Festival)
475	  with Nuits d'Afrique brushing its first weekend — a real multi-festival
476	  cluster; Toronto's autumn slot dodges TIFF entirely.
477	
478	### Netflix Is A Joke — maximum scale, biennial, and an anti-planner FAQ
479	
480	- **Biennial, not annual**: editions
481	  [2022, 2024, 2026 — no 2023 or 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix_Is_a_Joke_Festival)
482	  (a resale SEO site wearing a 2025 name misleads searches). Corporate-run
483	  by Netflix; 4–10 May 2026 delivered.
484	- **Scale**: its own site banner claims "475+ shows, 500+ artists, 45+
485	  venues… the largest comedy event in history"; the schedule page's inlined
486	  dataset carries **498 dated events across 116 venue slugs**, peaking at
487	  **101 events on the Saturday** — numerically the hardest clash problem in
488	  US comedy, spread across greater LA from the Hollywood Bowl to the Intuit
489	  Dome, where cross-town same-night stacking is impractical. Attendees treat
490	  it as pick-your-headliner anyway.
491	- **Ticketing**: the FAQ is explicit — "there are no festival passes"; 498
492	  events fan out to **12+ vendors** (counted from its own payload:
493	  Ticketmaster 167, Eventbrite 118, ShowClix 51, TicketWeb 34, …).
494	- **Data**: paradoxically the easiest big scrape in the US — a Next.js site
495	  that **inlines the entire event dataset (1.4MB) in the server-rendered
496	  payload** of [/schedule](https://www.netflixisajokefest.com/schedule):
497	  per-event times, venue ids, ticket URLs, per-venue lat/long, capacity,
498	  even parking and bag policy. One HTML fetch gives everything.
499	- **Planner field**: no official app; the site's favourites are the only
500	  tool, and no third party exists.
501	
502	### SF Sketchfest — fringe breadth, one-off depth
503	
504	[Founded 2001 and still run by its three founders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SF_Sketchfest);
505	annual each Jan/Feb (a COVID gap 2021–22), 23rd edition in 2026: **200+
506	shows, 500+ performers, 13 venues, 18 days** (per
507	[Deadline](https://deadline.com/)). The catch that decides its shape: the
508	programming is **reunions, tributes and one-night specials that structurally
509	cannot repeat** (a *Brain Candy* 30th anniversary, "The Women of SNL") — ~11
510	shows/day of unresolvable clashes, since nothing gets a second chance.
511	Tickets per show via a single
512	[Eventbrite organizer account](https://www.eventbrite.com/o/sf-sketchfest-57967098043);
513	planning outsourced to a yearly [Sched instance](https://sfsketchfest2026.sched.com/);
514	the festival's own site is bot-walled (SiteGround captcha), making Eventbrite
515	the practical machine surface.
516	
517	### Moontower — the US festival with a fringe inside it
518	
519	Run by the nonprofit [Paramount Theatre](https://www.austintheatre.org/moontower-comedy/)
520	(Austin Theatre Alliance) each April since 2012. Two tiers: two weeks of
521	theatre headliners on single tickets (Tessitura, the venue's own system) —
522	and the **4-day Club Binge**, where a **badge is walk-in access to 10+
523	walkable downtown clubs, no tickets or reservations**, 100+ comedians
524	playing multiple showcase slots. That binge is genuine fringe mechanics
525	(turn-up-and-graze, room-capacity risk instead of ticket clashes) — the
526	closest any US major comes. Note the census-table caveat: the "12 days"
527	overstates the fringe-like part; the binge is four.
528	
529	### SXSW Comedy — a garnish on a badge mega-festival
530	
531	[Since 2008](https://sxsw.com/festivals/comedy/), but tiny: the official
532	stats block for 2027 says **"4 nights, 2 venues, 65+ performers, 30 shows"**
533	— all included with an SXSW badge ($550–$1,395 tiers), no per-show tickets.
534	Comedy barely clashes with itself; it clashes with the 1,000+ music
535	showcases, film premieres and conference tracks on the same credential — the
536	purest "the city is the draw" case in the census, and the reason SXSW ships
537	the circuit's best official planner
538	([SXSW GO on Eventbase](https://www.eventbase.com/sxsw-go) + schedule.sxsw.com).
539	
540	### New York Comedy Festival, and the November pile-up
541	
542	[Founded 2004 by Caroline Hirsch and still produced by Carolines / 550
543	Comedy Inc.](https://nycomedyfestival.com/faq/) — "10 days, 5 boroughs,
544	100+ shows, 200+ comedians" grown to 150+ by August: headliner one-nighters
545	(Beacon, Town Hall, Kings Theatre, a Stand Up for Heroes gala) over ~39
546	venues with **per-venue ticketing** (Ticketmaster / ATG / house systems) and
547	open submissions confined to three contest-style showcases. Data note: a
548	live WordPress REST API
549	([/wp-json/wp/v2/lineup](https://nycomedyfestival.com/wp-json/wp/v2/lineup?per_page=2))
550	makes it scrapable without a browser. Its window sits in the **US November
551	pile-up**: NYCF (6–15), 312 Chicago (5–15), Boston (10–14) and Skankfest
552	New Orleans (13–15) all overlap, circulating the same touring headliners
553	through different cities.
554	
555	### The promoter slates and the rest, briefly
556	
557	- **[Nashville Comedy Festival](https://www.nashcomedyfest.com/)** and
558	  **[312 Comedy Festival](https://www.312comedyfestival.com/)** (Chicago)
559	  are both "presented by Outback Presents" — a promoter's April/November
560	  booking slate wearing a festival name: arena and theatre one-nighters plus
561	  club weekends, per-venue ticketing (Etix/AXS/Ticketmaster counted in the
562	  hundreds of links on their own pages). 312's Zanies club weekends — the
563	  same comic doing 2 shows a night for a weekend — are the nearest thing to
564	  a "run" in US club culture.
565	- **[Boston Comedy Festival](https://www.bostoncomedyfest.com/)** (26th
566	  year) is **competition-spined**: open submissions, ~96 comics through
567	  bracket rounds to a Somerville Theatre final — fringe-adjacent spirit,
568	  contest schedule.
569	- **[Skankfest](https://skankfest.com/)** (GaS Digital) is the
570	  **anti-planner**: one venue compound, pass-only (Tixr), 11am–midnight
571	  overlapping sets — and **"the full festival schedule will be released the
572	  day of the festival"**. Fans buy the brand, not a lineup; sold out seven
573	  years running. Roving city history (Queens → Houston → Las Vegas → New
574	  Orleans).
575	- **[Del Close Marathon](https://ucbcomedy.com/)** (UCB, NYC): **56
576	  nonstop hours** of improv across six stages in two venues on a badge —
577	  round-the-clock grazing, structurally one continuous show.
578	- **[NY Laughs Fest](https://nylaughsfest.com/)** (2nd year, nonprofit):
579	  free public-space comedy (Union Square) plus 20+ club shows — a civic
580	  showcase.
581	
582	### The UK & Ireland showcase belt, briefly
583	
584	- **[Galway Comedy Festival](https://galwaycomedyfestival.ie/)** — "Ireland's
585	  largest comedy festival" by its own meta description, ex-"Vodafone Comedy
586	  Carnival": a curated headliner week each October
587	  ([69 shows / 16 venues in 2025, per RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/culture/2025/0911/1533013-galway-comedy-festival-reveals-2025-line-up-ahead-of-october-bash/)),
588	  grown out of the Róisín Dubh venue, ~10 shows/day. Self-run ticketing on a
589	  custom SPA built with Base44 (an AI app-builder) — which also exposes its
590	  operator admin routes in the page shell.
591	- **The "Dublin Comedy Festival" untangled** — the tracker's 23-day September
592	  entry links to what
593	  [redirects to dublincomedyfestival.ie](https://www.dublincomedyfestival.ie/),
594	  whose own headline is "**West Dublin's Comedy Takeover**": ~20 shows of the
595	  same few acts rotating suburban pubs and hotels (Reginald D Hunter ×4
596	  nights), per-event tickets on Universe. It is a rebranded pub circuit, not
597	  a fringe — the census's second-longest UK entry dissolves on inspection.
598	  Dublin's real big comedy event is the
599	  [Paddy Power Comedy Festival](https://aikenpromotions.com/show/paddy-power-comedy-festival/)
600	  (Aiken Promotions, Iveagh Gardens, four days each July); September in
601	  Dublin belongs to the theatre-led
602	  [Dublin Fringe](https://www.fringefest.com/news/dublin-fringe-festival) —
603	  the likely source of the label confusion.
604	- **[Aberdeen Comedy Festival](https://www.aberdeenperformingarts.com/aberdeen-comedy-festival/)**
605	  — the venue-trust model: Aberdeen Performing Arts (the charity running the
606	  Music Hall, His Majesty's and The Lemon Tree) programmes a curated
607	  three-weekend season (19 Sep–4 Oct 2026, Russell Howard, Susan Calman) on
608	  its own Spektrix box office. A handful of shows a night; no clash problem.
609	  The census's 16-day length flatters it — it is three weekends, not a run.
610	- **[Wells Comedy Festival](https://www.wellscomfest.com/)** — the curated
611	  small-town weekend: produced by Plosive (the podcast company), 10th
612	  edition 2026, three walkable rooms in England's smallest city, big-name
613	  bills (Acaster, Pascoe, Kumar), TicketSource ticketing.
614	- **[Greenwich Comedy Garden](https://www.greenwichcomedygarden.co.uk/)** —
615	  tracker correction: rebranded from "Greenwich Comedy Festival" (the old
616	  domain redirects). Producer 57 Festivals' five-night big-top residency at
617	  the Old Royal Naval College — mixed-bill headliner nights, See Tickets —
618	  and the same team runs Brighton/Cambridge/Norwich Comedy Gardens: a
619	  **replicated single-site format**, the UK's polite cousin of the Great
620	  Outdoors model below.
621	- **[Roundhouse Comedy Festival](https://www.roundhouse.org.uk/seasons/roundhouse-comedy-festival/)**
622	  — tracker correction: 2026 actually ran **1–18 August** (not 23–26), one
623	  Camden building, curated with Berk's Nest, headline one-nighters and live
624	  podcasts on the venue's own box office — a single-building season that
625	  deliberately counter-programs the Edinburgh month.
626	- **[London Clown Festival](https://www.londonclownfest.online/)** (tracker's
627	  domain is dead; this is the live one) — niche curated clown/physical
628	  programme split between Soho Theatre and Jacksons Lane, each on its own
629	  box office. The census's 15-day length is two venues' seasons, not a
630	  dense festival.
631	
632	### Dubai Comedy Festival — the destination-marketing umbrella
633	
634	- **Organizer**: a government-backed promoter consortium — [BRAG "partnered
635	  with DTCM (Dubai's tourism department) and Live Nation to bring back the
636	  festival" in 2020](https://brag.world/dubai-comedy-festival); recent editions
637	  are presented by Dubai Calendar and produced by BRAG, Live Nation, GME
638	  Events and DXB Live (per [Katch International](https://katchinternational.com/)).
639	  Annual since the 2020 revival, 7th edition in 2026, grown from 4 days to 10.
640	- **Scale & model**: ["50+ artists, 40+ shows, 3+ venues"](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/about)
641	  over 10 days — one-night international touring acts (Mo Gilligan, Katherine
642	  Ryan, Vir Das…), many "presented by" third-party promoters under the
643	  festival umbrella, deliberately multilingual (English, Arabic, Hindi, Urdu,
644	  Russian), plus a small up-and-comers sidebar ("Comedy Bizarre").
645	- **Venues & clash**: spread across a car-scale city — Dubai Opera, Coca-Cola
646	  Arena, Mall of the Emirates theatre, clubs; 2–3 shows per evening across
647	  distant venues. Lineup-picking with traffic, not a schedule grid.
648	- **Ticketing & data**: per-show, multi-vendor — mostly
649	  [Platinumlist](https://dubaicomedyfestival.platinumlist.net/) (which runs an
650	  aggregating microsite), plus venue box offices and Ticketmaster.ae for some
651	  shows. The [shows page](https://www.dubaicomedyfest.ae/shows) is
652	  server-rendered Squarespace carrying every show's date, venue, language,
653	  price and vendor link in plain HTML — the easiest large-festival page to
654	  read mechanically in the whole census.
655	
656	## The structural exhibits
657	
658	Festivals that mark out the edges of the taxonomy — none is a planner market,
659	and each pins down one shape the census keeps producing.
660	
661	### Great Outdoors Comedy Festival — the music-festival pole, confirmed
662	
663	The hypothesis the census raised, confirmed and then some: GOCF is not even a
664	serial tour but a **franchise running parallel one-stage city productions on
665	shared weekends** — [seven 2026 stops](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/):
666	Edmonton *and* Winnipeg both 17–19 July, Calgary *and* Vancouver 28–30 August
667	with Spokane the same weekend, Halifax 6–9 August, Mississauga 11–13
668	September; 2027 dates already on sale. Owned and run by
669	[Trixstar](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/about), an Edmonton
670	promoter; since 2021 it claims 400,000+ cumulative attendees. One outdoor
671	stage per city (Vancouver's Stanley Park permit caps at
672	[10,000/day](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/the-great-outdoors-comedy-festival-proposal-stanley-park)),
673	two shows a day (matinee + evening), each a one-off bill of touring headliners
674	(Bill Burr, Matt Rife, Pete Davidson tiers), grounds cleared between shows,
675	explicitly [no application process](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/gocf-faqs)
676	for performers, GA/VIP tiers, no re-entry, 18+/19+. Ticketing is
677	[Tixr-only](https://greatoutdoorscomedyfestival.com/cities/vancouver); the
678	Webflow site is fully server-rendered. **Scheduling problem: none by design —
679	the only decision is which city you are in.** This is what "comedy festival"
680	means when the shape is literally a music festival's.
681	
682	### The TV-taping festivals — Winnipeg and Halifax
683	
684	Canada's two legacy festivals are shaped end to end by broadcast production,
685	and they show what a "festival" is when its real product is television:
686	
687	- **[Winnipeg Comedy Festival](https://www.winnipegcomedyfestival.com/about-us)**
688	  (annual since 2002, produced by the nonprofit Gas Station Arts Centre):

# The festival circuits

The world's comedy festivals as a market: what exists, what shape each one is,
and what it would take to point EdFringeNow's planning product at any of them.
This page exists because the owner's direction (2026-09-01) is to grow
EdFringeNow into a festival-planning product, and the first expansion axis is
the art form the product already serves best — comedy is the Fringe's largest
genre. Compiled once, refined in place.

Division of labour with the neighbouring pages:
[festmaxxing-environments/](../festmaxxing-environments/README.md)
owns the *city* question (which cities carry the Edinburgh-in-August overwhelm
pattern, whatever the art form); this page owns the *comedy festival* question —
the worldwide circuit, each festival's structure, organizer, ticketing and data
reachability — plus a deliberately light survey of the **film** festivals that
share the planner-complex shape (its own section below). Planner-type
competitors found along the way live on
[competitor-landscape/](../competitor-landscape/README.md).

## Key insights

- Only ~8 of 85 census festivals are fringe-shaped. Most of the circuit is one-night showcases with nothing to schedule.
- MICF is the southern Edinburgh — 803 shows, 9,164 performances, open registration — with unauthenticated JSON APIs.
- Leicester's operator went bust in Aug 2026 owing performers ticket money. Feb 2027 is two rival reboots.
- Nearly everything is annual in the same city, but brands churn: JFL survived receivership, Netflix Is A Joke is biennial.
- Recurrence decides planning — in film too: Fringe shows play ~14 times, Berlinale screens films up to 5×, US one-offs are terminal.
- Leicester and Brighton share one platform (Eventotron) and identical open APIs — one adapter reads both.
- No machine-readable comedy-festival calendar exists. The best tracker is one journalist's hand-kept page.

## The census: a year of comedy festivals

The seed source is the festival tracker kept by From The Comic's Comic
([fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/](https://fromthecomicscomic.com/comedy-festivals/),
fetched 2026-09-01), which lists the circuit by month for 2026 with a stated
confirmation policy — "If it's not listed, it's not confirmed yet." The full
2026 list, with run lengths computed from its dates:

| Festival | 2026 dates | Days | City |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SF Sketchfest | 15 Jan – 1 Feb | 18 | San Francisco, US |
| Leicester Comedy Festival | 4–22 Feb | 19 | Leicester, UK |
| SoWal Comedy Festival | 12–14 Feb | 3 | South Walton FL, US |
| Just For Laughs Vancouver | 12–22 Feb | 11 | Vancouver, CA |
| Adelaide Fringe | 20 Feb – 22 Mar | 31 | Adelaide, AU |
| Black Women in Comedy Laff Fest | 25 Feb – 1 Mar | 5 | Brooklyn NY, US |
| Vice City Comedy Festival | 26–28 Feb | 3 | Miami FL, US |
| SLO Comedy Festival | 26 Feb – 1 Mar | 4 | San Luis Obispo CA, US |
| Toronto Sketch Comedy Festival | 4–15 Mar | 12 | Toronto, CA |
| West End Comedy Festival | 6–8 Mar | 3 | Atlanta GA, US |
| Gilda's LaughFest | 11–15 Mar | 5 | Grand Rapids MI, US |
| Sprung! | 12–15 Mar | 4 | Silver Spring MD, US |
| SXSW (comedy) | 13–16 Mar | 4 | Austin TX, US |
| Toledano Street Comedy Festival | 19–22 Mar | 4 | New Orleans LA, US |
| JFL Belgium | 23–29 Mar | 7 | Belgium, BE |
| Melbourne International Comedy Festival | 25 Mar – 19 Apr | 26 | Melbourne, AU |
| Bergamot Comedy Festival | 24–28 Mar | 5 | Santa Monica CA, US |
| DC Sketchfest | 25–28 Mar | 4 | Washington DC, US |
| Lil Rhody Laugh Riot | 26–29 Mar | 4 | Providence RI, US |
| Riot Comedy Festival | 1–4 Apr | 4 | Houston TX, US |
| Asheville Comedy Festival | 3–4 Apr | 2 | Asheville NC, US |
| YALL Comedy Fest | 8–10 Apr | 3 | New York NY, US |
| Big Pine Comedy Festival | 8–11 Apr | 4 | Chandler AZ, US |
| Moontower Comedy Festival | 8–19 Apr | 12 | Austin TX, US |
| Nashville Comedy Festival | 9–19 Apr | 11 | Nashville TN, US |
